# Magic Notifications Plugin

Notifications for the Magic Framework: the `Notify` facade over a backend-driven inbox (`DatabaseChannel`, `NotificationPoller`, `NotificationManager`), a self-addressed `PushChannel`, OneSignal push (`OneSignalDriver` mobile, `OneSignalWebDriver` web), realtime delivery over `magic_socket`, ready-made list, preferences and bell widgets, and the `notifications:*` dowel commands. There is no mail channel.

**Version:** 1.2.1 · **Dart:** >=3.13.0 · **Flutter:** >=3.47.0 · **Requires:** `magic` ^1.0.0, `magic_socket` ^1.0.0, `dowel` ^1.0.0

## Commands

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `flutter test --coverage` | Run all tests with coverage |
| `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos` | Static analysis |
| `dart format .` | Format all code |
| `flutter pub publish --dry-run` | Pre-publish check |
| `python3 tool/check-docs.py` | Docs structure, links, fragments and ToC anchors; run it after any `doc/`, `README.md` or `llms.txt` change |

The package has no `bin/`: its commands run as `dart run magic:dowel notifications:<command>` in a host app, after `plugin:install`.

## Architecture

```
lib/
├── magic_notifications.dart        # Barrel export, the only public runtime API
├── cli.dart                        # Barrel with the dowel provider only, for a pure Dart dispatcher
└── src/
    ├── notification_manager.dart   # Singleton: channels, driver registry, identity reconcile, polling, realtime, stream
    ├── notification_poller.dart    # Timer with pause and resume
    ├── channels/                   # DatabaseChannel (send is a no-op), PushChannel (self-addressed, off by default)
    ├── drivers/push/               # PushDriver contract, OneSignalDriver, OneSignalWebDriver, JS interop
    ├── drivers/push_web/           # onesignal_factory.dart: conditional-import arms (_io, _web, _stub)
    ├── http/                       # NotificationsListController, NotificationPreferencesController
    ├── support/                    # PushStateReporter (Notify.pushState), NotificationLog
    ├── ui/                         # NotificationViewRegistry, list and preferences views, NotificationDropdown, PushPrompt
    └── cli/                        # MagicNotificationsDowelProvider, commands/, support/xcode_configurations.dart

install.yaml                        # Provider injection only; the dynamic install is InstallCommand's override
assets/stubs/install/               # notification_config.stub, OneSignal web worker and script stubs
example/                            # Runnable app: boots the provider and shows what works without a backend
doc/                                # User docs, published by the docs site: getting-started/, basics/, architecture/
skills/magic-notifications/         # Agent skill, installed with `npx skills add anilcancakir/magic_notifications`
tool/check-docs.py                  # Offline docs gate, run by docs-link-check.yml
```

## Post-Change Checklist

After any source code change, sync **before committing**. A change is not done while one of these is stale:

1. **`CHANGELOG.md`**: Add entry under `[Unreleased]` section
2. **`README.md`, `llms.txt` and the `doc/` pages**: Update if features, API, or usage changes
3. **`skills/magic-notifications/SKILL.md`**: Update when the API, a rule or a gotcha changes; its `version:` moves with the release, and the publish check compares it with the tag
4. **`CLAUDE.md`**: Update the architecture tree when files move
5. **`example/`**: Keep `lib/main.dart` calling the real API

## Development Flow (TDD)

Every feature, fix, or refactor goes through red-green-refactor: write a failing test, write the minimum code to pass it, then clean up with the tests green. No production code without a failing test first; `flutter test`, `dart analyze` and `dart format .` stay clean after every change.

## Testing

- `Http.fake(<String, MagicResponse>{...})` stubs the backend; `PushChannel` ships off, so a test of it sets `notifications.push.self_test_enabled` with `Config.set` first
## Key Gotchas

| Mistake | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| Adding a mail channel, or reading `toMail`, `notifiableEmail` or the `mail` config block | The runtime reads none of them; `test --channel mail` and the `channels` mail block carry the leftovers, and an older generated config may still hold a `mail` block. Do not extend them |
| Importing `OneSignalDriver` or `OneSignalWebDriver` from the provider | Go through `createOneSignalDriver()` in `onesignal_factory.dart`; each build compiles only the arm it can run |
| Assuming `markAsRead` rolls back on an HTTP error | Magic's `Http` returns a `MagicResponse` for an error status; the refetch runs only when the call throws |
| Reading `{data: {count}}` or sending `per_page` | `unreadCount` reads top-level `count` and `fetchPaginatedNotifications` sends `perPage`; change both sides together, with `doc/basics/laravel-backend-setup.md` |
| Calling `registerDefault` on `Notify.view` from outside | It is `@internal`; use `register`, and `hasOverride` rather than `has` to ask whether the host chose |
| Declaring the push identity inside this package | `magic_starter` owns it; an app without the starter calls `Notify.initializePush` and `logoutPush` itself |
| Importing Flutter or the runtime barrel into `lib/cli.dart` | The dowel dispatcher is a pure Dart process |
| Bumping `pubspec.yaml` without `magicNotificationsVersion` | `lib/src/cli/notifications_dowel_provider.dart` prints it in every command banner; the install test fails on a mismatch |
| Relative paths in `pubspec_overrides.yaml` | Use absolute ones; the file is never committed |

## Release

1. Open a `release:` PR that bumps `pubspec.yaml`, `skills/magic-notifications/SKILL.md`, the `Version:` line above and `magicNotificationsVersion`, and promotes `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md`.
2. After it merges, tag the merge commit with the bare version (`git tag 1.0.1 && git push origin 1.0.1`, no `v`). `publish.yml` runs from the tag; the pub.dev Admin tab holds repository `anilcancakir/magic_notifications`, tag pattern `{{version}}` and push events only (re-enter it after a repository transfer).
3. A failed `validate` is fixed forward: delete the tag (`git push --delete origin <tag>` and `git tag -d <tag>`), fix it on a PR and tag the new merge commit. If only `github-release` fails after pub.dev accepted the version, use "Re-run failed jobs" (never "Re-run all jobs") or `gh release create <tag> --title <tag> --latest --verify-tag --notes-file <file>`.

## CI

- `ci.yml`: push/PR → `flutter pub get` → `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos` → `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` → `flutter test --coverage` → codecov upload
- `changelog.yml`: a PR that changes `lib/`, `install.yaml` or `assets/stubs/` must also change `CHANGELOG.md`; Dependabot, `release:` PRs and the `skip-changelog` label are exempt
- `docs-link-check.yml`: every PR runs `python3 tool/check-docs.py` and an offline lychee pass; Mondays an external-link pass
- `publish.yml`: tag on master → version stamps (tag, pubspec, skill) → analyze, format, test, dry-run, pana 160/160, changelog section → OIDC publish → GitHub Release
